newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli troops, Palestinians clash in West Bank.
newsitem.headline: Israeli troops, Palestinians clash in West Bank.

text.p: Israeli troops clashed with Palestinians stoning them in the West Bank on Saturday in a 10th day of clashes spurred by Israel's building a settlement in Arab East Jerusalem, witnesses said.
Israeli radio stations said troops shooting rubber bullets wounded at least four Palestinians stoning their position at a Jewish shrine on the outskirts of Bethlehem West Bank enclave.
Witnesses said that demonstrators burned a doll with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's name scrawled on it during the Bethlehem clash.
At one point, Palestinians lobbed stones over a bus full of foreign tourists as it passed between them and the Israeli soldiers, witnesses said.
Israeli troops firing rubber bullets wounded two more Palestinians during clashes near Bir Zeit village north of Ramallah West Bank self-rule enclave, witnesses there said.

At the outskirts of Ramallah, Palestinian police used clubs to force back demonstrators trying to reach Israeli positions and held them back briefly. The Palestinian security forces linked arms forming a human barrier to block the protesters who eventually forced their way past and began hurling stones.
Peace moves between the Palestinians and Israel plunged into crisis this month after Israel broke ground on the settlement and an Islamist suicide bombing in Tel Aviv that killed three Israelis.
